summary: Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock. She served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shu-fen Liu works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She held posts at Academia Sinica (attested 2012), including as professor at the Institute of History and Philology (attested 2018).

Shubhachandra is an Indologist who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and held a post in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned his BA at Komazawa University (~1961–1965), where he studied under Shigeo Kamata (~1961–1966), and later served as professor at Komazawa University (attested 1988–2016).
Shudo Iwai (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Komazawa University. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1988).

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (~1919–1923) and Zhejiang University, and served as director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1944–1982).

Shuji Takayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003), a commissioned researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), and a researcher at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Musashino University (2006).

Shujun Motegi specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned an MA at Banaras Hindu University (1973–1975) studying under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and an MA from Kyoto University (completed 1977), later serving as professor of ethics at Shinshu University (attested 2010).

Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who did graduate studies at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He served at Komazawa University as research assistant (attested 1973–1978) and professor (attested 1994), and held a post at Aichi Gakuin University.
Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under traditional teacher Wei Chueh and completed a PhD at Northwestern University in 2014 under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1950–1954) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1961), and later served as professor at Komazawa University (~1965–2001).
Shun'ei Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Otani University as a term-limited assistant professor until 2013 and as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1949–1986), where he became emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976) at Shuchiin University.
Shunpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1940–1943) and later held an academic post at Kyoto University (~1953–1984).

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Gyokujun So-on, Ian Kishizawa, and at Komazawa University (~1926–1930). He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe (born 1939) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, where he was a professor (~2004).
Shunshō Terakawa (1928–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1955). He later served as an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 1998–2006).
Shuntaro Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2011 and worked there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1971–1995) and held posts at Tama Art University and Kokugakuin University.
